natural_language_summary: TrafficA3a has environment-controlled car sensors carA and carB and system-controlled lights greenA and greenB. If a car is waiting at A while greenA is false, carA must remain true in the next step; the same condition applies to B. Infinitely often, not both car sensors are true. The system must never make both lights green at the same time.
modeling_decisions: The fixed signature was used exactly as supplied.
The waiting-car persistence requirements were modeled as environment safety assumptions because carA and carB are environment variables.
The liveness requirement that not both cars are present infinitely often was modeled as an environment justice assumption.

The initial draft was realizable but non-well-separated. To repair this without weakening stated environment assumptions, a system safety guarantee was added: whenever both car sensors are true, at least one light is green. Together with mutual exclusion, this means exactly one light is green in that state.
unresolved_ambiguities: The natural-language system guarantee explicitly states only mutual exclusion. The added service-when-both-wait guarantee is a well-separation repair that makes the stated environment assumptions feasible under conforming system behavior.
